description.narrative:
As highlighted in evaluations of SDG4 (UNStats, 2022), we are still far behind in achieving quality education globally, with Covid19 further sharpening inequalities. For us, quality education globally can only be achieved if policy-makers take a global and learner-centred approach, in which students in secondary education are at the forefront of the policy making process. This project is aimed at facilitating mutual learning, cooperation and exchange on the future of education and to co-create a shared understanding of what this future entails for Europe, Africa and beyond. We want to pilot a cooperation which we started building in 2024 with our “Education 2040” project, where we interviewed student unions in Europe and Africa asking them their priorities related to (a) politicalclimate, (b) learning and teaching methods, (c) access to education and inclusion, (d) different types of education (e) governance in education and (f) the relationship between education and society. The project idea comes fromour need to learn from each other interms of participation and political activation, resilience and tools used for youth-led policy and advocacy, as well as building astrong foundation for cross-continental policy-based cooperation.
The project willrun from May 2025 to May 2026 and will foresee acycle of 7 virtual exchanges aimed at capacity building of both leadership and advocacy skills (e.g. achieving government recognition, building integrity in student governments), but also providing a spacefor policy co-creation on topics such as safety and security at school, decolonisation of education, active citizenship in TVET. Two national events in Zambia and Sierra Leone will see the participation of over 100 students. In September 2025 more than 150 students from the 10 provinces of Zambia will come together in a residential robust policy event on digital education, accessibility and inclusion and transition to society. In November 2025 a similar event will happen in Sierra Leone on the topic of gender equality and mental health. During both events, representatives from the partners will deliver sessions and gather intelligence for the policy process of the project. The project will culminate with a meeting in April 2026 in Belgium to showcase thepreliminary results, build more cooperation and amplify the student voice gathered throughout the project. A final policy report and activation tool will be published in May 2026, to start follow up.

participating-org.narrative:
The Zambia National Students Union (ZANASU) is the umbrella body representing student unions from institutions of higher learning across Zambia. It advocates for students' rights, promotes academic freedom, and fosters national and international collaboration to enhance education and student welfare.
Vision: To be a dynamic, inclusive, and influential student movement that empowers students and contributes to national development.
Mission: To unite, represent, and advocate for students by promotingaccess to quality education, policy engagement, and student empowerment while fostering collaboration with stakeholders in Zambia and beyond.
Objectives - To protect and defend students' rights within and outside Zambia. - To promote unity and solidarity among students from higher learning institutions. - To advocate for academic freedoms and equal access to education. - To engage in policy research to drive educational reforms. - To empower students through leadership training, cultural exchange, and extracurricular activities. - To raise awareness on challenges affecting students and influence decision-making processes. - To collaborate with local, regional, and international organizations to strengthen student advocacy and participation.
Values - Democracy and Representation: Ensuring all students have a voice in decision-making. - Integrity and Accountability: Upholding transparency in leadership and financial management. - Equality and Inclusivity: Advocating for gender balance, diversity, and non-discrimination. - Empowerment and Innovation: Providing capacity-building opportunities for students. - Solidarity and Collaboration: Strengthening partnerships with stakeholders for studentadvancement.
ZANASU remains committed to fostering a student-centered education system, advocating for policy reforms, and empowering the next generation of leaders in Zambia.
